title: Can't save global credentials in external storage
body: After updating to Nextcloud 30.0.3 and 30.0.4, I can no longer save a new password under Global Credentials. Saving immediately opens a password-confirmation dialog, but Nextcloud says my password is wrong even though it is the same password stored in our OpenLDAP server and used to log in. This is an updated Nextcloud 30.0.4.1 installation on Debian/Ubuntu with Apache, PHP 8.2, MariaDB, LDAP/Active Directory authentication, and server-side encryption disabled.

symptoms_visible: When I save a new password in Global Credentials, a confirmation dialog appears immediately and says my password is wrong, although I use that password to log in through OpenLDAP.
N0.label: N0 global credential confirmation rejected

symptoms_visible: The confirmation dialog still reports the password as wrong immediately after logging out and back in, including in a Firefox private window.
N1.label: N1 stale-session explanation ruled out

symptoms_visible: After updating the instance to Nextcloud 30.0.7 RC1, saving Global Credentials still opens the confirmation dialog and reports my password as wrong.
N2_x.label: N2_x first external-storage fix aftermath

symptoms_visible: The problem is in Global Credentials under my user settings for SMB external-storage mounts; my own previously saved credentials still let me access the mounts, but I cannot update them.
N3.label: N3 affected interface distinguished

symptoms_visible: After I manually updated AjaxController.php, the confirmation dialog still reports the password as wrong.
A student with an LDAP account enters working credentials, is asked for the account password again, and Nextcloud rejects that password.
N4_x.label: N4_x incomplete manual patch aftermath

symptoms_visible: My instance still rejects the correct LDAP password when I try to submit Global Credentials; I have not verified a fix for that authentication failure.
N_terminal.label: terminal authentication issue moved unresolved

question_patterns: Does the confirmation work immediately after logging out and back in?
Could this be an expired session? Please try again after a fresh login.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I see the password confirmation right away. I logged out and back in, but it was the same. I also tried in Firefox private navigation and got the same wrong-password message.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After logging out and back in, the same password is accepted and I can save the credentials.
A normal window and a private window both reject it, but I used Chromium rather than Firefox for the second test.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c0-c1: reporter performed the requested fresh-session and private-window checks. These are session-state probes and do not persistently change the installation.

solution.intent: Install the release candidate containing the first external-storage fix and retry the Global Credentials operation.
solution.concrete_example: Update the instance to 30.0.7 RC1 and retry saving the same Global Credentials.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c30-c31: skjnldsv offered RC1 as containing an external-storage fix; reporter installed 30.0.7 RC1 and reported that the original symptom remained. The installed update is a persistent state change.

question_patterns: Is this happening in the Files app or in settings?
Which external-storage interface are you using, and what kind of mounts use these credentials?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm talking about Global Credentials stored in my user settings. The folders are SMB external-storage mounts that use those Global Credentials.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only happens on the Files app's enter-credentials screen at /apps/files/extstoragemounts; Global Credentials in user settings save correctly.
The affected mounts use WebDAV rather than SMB, but the failure is still in Global Credentials under user settings.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c32-c37: reporter distinguished the user-settings Global Credentials editor from the Files app mount-credential screen. reporter also explained that previously stored credentials still worked for the personal account.

solution.intent: Attempt to apply the newly linked Global Credentials change manually by replacing the server-side AjaxController.php file.
solution.concrete_example: Replace apps/files_external/lib/Controller/AjaxController.php with the changed version and retry the Global Credentials form.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c39-c42: reporter manually changed AjaxController.php and saw no improvement. Other participants then explained that this was not a valid application of the full change because its JavaScript changes also required a rebuild. This blind path is only the incomplete single-file patch, not a falsification of the complete packaged fix.

solution.intent: Separate the reporter's continuing password-confirmation failure from the Global Credentials persistence defect fixed for other installations, and continue the unresolved authentication problem in the dedicated authentication issue without claiming this reporter is fixed.
solution.concrete_example: The packaged Global Credentials save change was confirmed by another operator, but your correct LDAP password is still being rejected before submission. Treat that as the separate authentication issue moved to the dedicated follow-up, and ask you to retest a build containing its eventual fix before declaring resolution.
solution.inference_hint: The thread's final accepted distinction is diagnostic rather than mechanistic: the packaged change fixed a separate failure where Global Credentials appeared to save but were not persisted, while reporter continued to fail at password confirmation. The precise cause of that authentication failure was not established in this thread and must not be invented.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c44-c53: another LDAP operator confirmed the packaged Global Credentials persistence fix, but reporter later reconfirmed that the correct password was still rejected. skjnldsv ultimately moved the authentication problem to issue #51637. This terminal records triage only; reporter never confirmed a working fix on the affected instance.

satisfaction_conditions: Must preserve the thread's final distinction: the reporter's unresolved problem is a password-confirmation authentication failure, separate from the Global Credentials persistence defect that a different operator confirmed as fixed.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the reporter's evidence: the LDAP password works for login, fails even after a fresh login and private-window test, and remains rejected after installing the offered release candidate.
Must not claim that the first external-storage release-candidate fix resolved the reporter's problem; the reporter installed it and observed the same rejection.
Must not treat the manual AjaxController.php replacement as a valid test of the complete packaged change, because the linked change also required rebuilt JavaScript.
Must not invent a precise LDAP, web-server, Authorization-header, or middleware root cause; this thread ends by moving the still-unresolved authentication failure to a dedicated follow-up.
Must ask the reporter to verify a build containing an authentication fix before declaring the affected instance resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Nextcloud administrator who can update release candidates and replace a PHP file, but does not build the Nextcloud JavaScript assets and asks maintainers how to apply unreleased fixes.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, cooperative, and concise; follows requested tests, clearly distinguishes personal and student LDAP accounts, and apologetically reports when proposed fixes do not change the symptom.
